subject: Retention segmentation, emergency purge runbook, and proof-of-deletion requests
messages:
From: Lauren Davis <lauren.davis@acmehealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify backup purge windows + deletion evidencing

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Security team here at Acme had a couple follow-ups we need to close before procurement moves forward:

- Can you confirm the timeline for backup snapshot purge across tiers (hot/warm/cold)? We need to understand the maximum window data could be present in backups after deletion.
- What is Redwood's runbook for a customer-initiated emergency purge (legal hold release or court order)? We need steps, estimated time-to-purge, and verification outputs.
- Are proof-of-deletion artifacts (audit records, checksum, snapshot ID) produced and retained separately? Our audit requires preserved proof for 7 years after deletion.
- Please attach the current DPA subprocessors list and call out any cross-border transfer paths for EU->US data.

I'm attaching a short SOC2 questionnaire we use. Can we get a reply by EOD next week?

Thanks,
Lauren Davis
Security Operations
Acme Health

Attachment: Acme-SOC2-questions.pdf

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Davis <lauren.davis@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify backup purge windows + deletion evidencing

Hi Lauren,

Appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers up front, and I looped in Legal (Kimberly) + Product Ops (Marissa) for the runbook details:

- Snapshot purge windows: we operate tiered snapshot retention. Typical configurations for hosted accounts are: hot snapshots (up to 14 days), warm (30–90 days depending on plan), cold/archival snapshots (retained up to 365 days unless a specific retention override is set). Backups in the Dedicated/Private deployments are configurable by the customer and governed by the committed retention term.
- Emergency purge: we have a documented deletion runbook that includes ticket creation, isolation of affected volumes, snapshot deregistration, S3 lifecycle enforcement, and a purge job that marks objects deleted and emits a proof artifact. Time-to-purge varies by data location — warm tier ~ minutes-hours, cold tier may require background archive job (hours-days).
- Proof-of-deletion: we generate an audit package that includes snapshot IDs, object manifests, deletion job run id, and signed digests. We currently surface those on request to customers and log them in the audit trail.
- Subprocessors: we maintain an up-to-date subprocessor registry; I'll attach a retention summary and Marissa will call out the cloud provider transfer paths.

Suggest a 30-min call next week to review the runbook and confirm any carveouts. Are you available Tue 11/24 or Mon 11/30?

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: retention-summary-PR-v1.pdf

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Lauren Davis <lauren.davis@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 11:03 AM Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Appreciate the clear asks. Quick answers up front...

Hi all,

A few legal points to ensure we have the right commitments and operational controls to satisfy Acme's audit:

1) Retention carveouts: we can offer configurable retention windows per data class. For PII/PHI, propose default warm snapshot purge at 30 days and archival purge at 180 days unless Acme requests a longer commit in the DPA addendum.
2) Emergency purge runbook: the runbook needs an explicit legal-hold escalation path. I propose the following mandatory steps be added to the runbook:
   - Written eradication request from Acme legal (email + ticket)
   - Legal hold check: system prevents purge if active hold exists; legal team provides clearance when applicable
   - Purge: snapshot deregistration, object-level expunge via secure delete, key rotation where applicable
   - Verification: cryptographic digest, signed by Redwood with timestamp, and retention of the verification artifact for 7 years in read-only archive for audit.
3) Subprocessor addendum: Acme asks for a dedicated subprocessor SLA for their region. We can draft an addendum but need product sign-off on the longer retention of proof artifacts.

I'll attach suggested redlines and a checklist of what must be included in a compliant proof-of-deletion package.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: legal-retention-carveouts.docx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Lauren Davis <lauren.davis@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 14:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify backup purge windows + deletion evidencing

On Sun, Nov 22, 2026 at 08:15 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> A few legal points to ensure we have the right commitments...

Thanks Kim — noted. Lauren / Acme team, below are the concrete ops notes that map to the legal checklist and how we can automate evidence collection:

- Snapshots & backups:
  * Hot (primary runtime) snapshots: retained 14 days by default. Purge job runs hourly for expired objects.
  * Warm snapshots: default 30 days; TTL enforced by lifecycle tag "retention:30d" and background reclamation job.
  * Cold archive snapshots: tagged "retention:180d" (configurable up to 365d). These are stored in immutable cold buckets (object lock) until TTL expiry unless an approved legal purge is executed.
- Emergency purge workflow (technical):
  1) Create incident ticket (P0) with customer-supplied legal authorization; ticket triggers isolation of account replicas.
  2) Flag snapshots with a purge marker, queue deletion jobs for both S3 object delete and snapshot metadata purge.
  3) Run secure-delete that issues a deletion manifest: snapshot IDs, object keys, deletion timestamps, run id.
  4) Sign manifest with HSM-backed key and upload artifact to our audit archive (read-only).
  5) Emit a verification report to customer and create a signed DOI (deletion-of-information) record.
- Proof storage: Proof artifacts are kept in a separate immutable audit bucket (7-year retention by default for hosted enterprise customers).
- Cross-border transfers & subprocessors: our primary cloud provider acts as a subprocessor (provider-name redacted for thread), with data movement for EU to US happening only when customer opts into multi-region failover. We can restrict failover for Acme to keep EU-data-in-region; that will be captured in the DPA addendum.

Operational asks for Acme to confirm:
- Desired warm and cold TTLs (we suggest 30 / 180 to start).
- Whether Acme requires the 7-year preservation of proof artifacts (default for enterprise is 7 years; confirm).

We have a draft runbook at the drive link and can walk through on the call. Proposed call: Mon 12/05 10:00 AM PT.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Davis <lauren.davis@acmehealth.com>

Priya / team,

Thanks for the detailed runbook and for surfacing the legal redlines. Acme is comfortable moving forward with the following on the condition we get the documented artifacts and a subprocessor addendum for our EU region:

- Retention windows: warm 30 days, cold 180 days.
- Emergency purge: follow the runbook steps listed by Marissa. We require a signed proof-of-deletion package after purge, with cryptographic digest and the DOI record.
- Proof artifacts: Acme confirms it needs those artifacts retained for 7 years in read-only form for audit purposes.
- Subprocessor addendum: please provide a short addendum that prevents cross-border failover of Acme EU data without prior written consent.

We accept the proposed call time Mon 12/05 10:00 AM PT to walk through any final items and capture the addendum scope. See you then.

Regards,
Lauren Davis
Security Operations
Acme Health
